The main takeaway from our work is that

the right to refuse life-sustaining treatment is a relative right that can be overridden by other considerations, and that it should be respected only to the extent that it does not interfere with the interests of others.

the courts' presumption in favour of life-saving treatment, which is based on the principle that life should be preserved, should be replaced by a presumption in favour or against life-saving treatment, based on the principle of respecting the patient's autonomy.
